messages.content: Write the introduction to a monthly engineering newsletter whose theme this month is technical debt. Around 200 words.

output:
Here's the intro (~215 words), with an author-name placeholder in the middle paragraph:

---

Nobody schedules technical debt. It arrives the way a second mortgage does: one reasonable decision at a time, each defensible on the Tuesday it was made.

This month we're looking at what those Tuesdays add up to.

The framing we usually reach for is guilt. Someone cut a corner, and now we pay. That's mostly wrong. A lot of the debt in any mature system was the right call at the time. You shipped the hardcoded region list because the alternative was missing the launch, and the launch mattered more than the list. The mistake isn't the shortcut. It's that we almost never write down the interest rate.

So this issue is about accounting. **[Author]** on why the payments API took eleven months to untangle, and what the first estimate got wrong. A short piece on the migrations we abandoned halfway: six of them, still sitting in the schema. And a proposal from the platform team for tracking debt as a line item in planning, instead of as a feeling people have in retros.

One thing worth saying up front. Not all of it should be paid off. Some debt you carry to the end of the system's life, on purpose, and knowing which is most of the work.
